# THE FRUSTRATION → buildout (Claude, 2026-07-13 → 07-16) — produced OD-REDESIGN-56..66

---

## 🧑 OWNER (verbatim)

```text
im working on the redesign and ask the same question to 2 agents. i need you to assess which of these agents answer better? and how to prioritize the follow up implementation going forward. 

this was my concern:
the redesign produces mockup after 50+ grilling QnA but ended having to be in multi iterations process to get something im not repulse with, not happy enough, but passable. 

this is the prompt/question to the AGENT-1:
<AGENT1-Q>
i put back your redesign work back to the initial agent and ask to review it. it says the following:
------
The other agent correctly identified a major source of your discomfort, but its claim that the problems are “all addressed” is too optimistic.

The missing feeling is primarily interaction grammar: E7 contains familiar-looking components, but they do not consistently behave like familiar software.

What the agent correctly identified:

- Collection, saved-view, and presentation controls looked identical despite changing different things.
- Work lacked a stable “one noun per page” structure.
- Rina’s empty default was a poor role-aware choice.
- Jargon, inconsistent unread counts, duplicate copy, and dual completion controls added friction.

Those changes noticeably improved Work. [[The revised desktop screen](https://claude.ai/Users/ariefsaid/Coding/gordi-mos-e7-prototype/output/playwright/e7-audit-work-rina.png)](</Users/ariefsaid/Coding/gordi-mos-e7-prototype/output/playwright/e7-audit-work-rina.png>) is more scannable than the previous pill matrix.

But the revision changed the appearance of conventional navigation without implementing conventional navigation:

1. Every Work collection still links to `#/work`.

   Tasks, Process Runs, Standards, and Signals have no distinct URL. In browser testing, I opened Process Runs and pressed Back; Back exited the app to `about:blank` instead of returning to Tasks. Refresh, bookmark, new-tab, and history therefore do not preserve the page the user believes they opened.

2. Work and Tasks are simultaneously shown as the current page.

   Both receive active styling and `aria-current="page"`. That is why the rail still feels subtly wrong: it presents two competing answers to “where am I?”

3. The rail is now overloaded.

   Opening Work adds four group headings and eight collections to an already substantial navigation rail. This pushes Modules down and makes Work structurally unlike every other destination. It resembles a standard SaaS rail, but the hierarchy has not been resolved.

4. The design remains object-first rather than job-first.

   Descriptions explain what “Process Runs” and “Standards” mean, but explanations are compensating for unclear entry points. A new user still has to decide which internal object represents what they want to accomplish.

5. Several actions remain generic.

   Process Runs, Projects, Objectives, and Follow-ups can still show `Create`, contrary to the locked contextual-action direction. These should say things such as “Start run,” “Create project,” or “Add follow-up.”

6. Mobile Work front-loads configuration.

   Before seeing actual work, the user encounters three selectors: Collection, Saved view, and View as. It is understandable, but it feels like configuring a database rather than starting work. See the [[phone comparison](https://claude.ai/Users/ariefsaid/Coding/gordi-mos-e7-prototype/output/playwright/e7-audit-phone-contact-sheet.png)](</Users/ariefsaid/Coding/gordi-mos-e7-prototype/output/playwright/e7-audit-phone-contact-sheet.png>).

Across all routes, the visual system is reasonably consistent. The unresolved structural discomfort is concentrated in Work and then echoed by inconsistent page grammars between Home, Work, Modules, Money, and Admin. The [[all-route desktop sheet](https://claude.ai/Users/ariefsaid/Coding/gordi-mos-e7-prototype/output/playwright/e7-audit-desktop-contact-sheet.png)](</Users/ariefsaid/Coding/gordi-mos-e7-prototype/output/playwright/e7-audit-desktop-contact-sheet.png>) makes that visible.

Why 50+ decisions did not prevent this: those decisions mostly define the domain and product rules—what objects exist, authority, visibility, lifecycle, and canonical records. They do not sufficiently define the reusable experience contract: navigation levels, URL semantics, default disclosure, component roles, page anatomy, and job-oriented entry points. D9 says “collection and saved-view grammar,” but not precisely how that grammar behaves.

My recommendation is:

- Preserve the domain decisions, fixtures, record renderers, Money, Inbox, authorization demonstrations, and scenario coverage.
- Stop incrementally patching the current shell.
- Replace the shell/workspace interaction layer once, preceded by a short binding Convention Contract.
- Give every Work collection a canonical route such as `/work/tasks`, `/work/runs`, and `/work/standards`.
- Put saved view and presentation state in URL parameters.
- Make Work a collapsible rail group or redirect to the user’s last collection; never show both parent and child as the current page.
- Define one reusable page anatomy and verb-object action convention across every route.
- Validate it with task-based usability walkthroughs, not only the static J/Scenario verifier.

The static verifier, syntax checks, `git diff --check`, console checks, and responsive rendering all pass. Those checks prove coverage and implementation integrity; they do not prove that the interface follows users’ learned conventions.

So: the critique found a real and important part of what you were sensing, but its fix treated the most visible symptom. Your remaining unease is justified. I would salvage the product model and records, but rebuild the navigation and workspace grammar before asking you to approve Phase 0. No files were changed during this review.

-----

to which i responded:

i think part of my discomfort is also the amount of different objects / components in the ui. it hsould push for more reusability. what is the difference between task, follow up and process runs? why not all as tasks? then the signal, why not its own rail? or why not at home? why at work? on signal, why the form so lengthy? i'm thinking the signal can take inspiration from a social media (fb) post updates. its simple to post, a text box, an icon to add image, top/bottom of text box there are pills (add location, add mention) and if you type @ in textbox, it pops up a fuzzy match search. the fuzzy match search would have the different category and show the category, so the user is easy to spot eg. Gordi HQ as location / Gordi HQ as team. etc. should  we do another drill-with-docs? but again i dont want another 50+ QnA that ended up not producing what i expected nor prevent the UI mishaps as this has been several iterations to get to this point. I'm also mindful of the fact, this is only mockup phase, we havent actually build this redesign. i havent event touched further aspects of the app, the roastery, the standards, and possible extensions like calendar of events happening around the outlets we managed etc. how to make this merry go round more efficient. lets discuss and plan this first.

-----
can we discuss here as well
</AGENT1-Q>
<AGENT1-A>
I'll take positions rather than survey options.

Why 55 decisions didn't prevent this (and what actually broke)
The grill produced domain law — what objects exist, who may act, what's versioned. That output is durable and I wouldn't reopen it. What nobody ever wrote down is the experience law: how many nouns the rail may show, what a URL means, what one page looks like, when configuration is visible vs hidden. Every builder invented those per round — that's the merry-go-round. The reviewer's point that my fix "changed the appearance of conventional navigation without implementing conventional navigation" is fair: real routes, one current-page answer, and collapsible hierarchy are exactly the kind of rules that were never anywhere in writing.

So: no, not another 50-question drill. The domain is drilled. What's missing is a 1–2 page binding Experience Contract — roughly ten falsifiable rules (URL semantics like /work/tasks?view=overdue, one page anatomy for every route, verb+object actions, chips=saved-views/segments=layout/rail=places, capture-first disclosure, a surface budget). Plus about eight owner calls on object surfacing — which you've essentially already raised yourself.

Your object questions — my positions
"Why not all as Tasks?" — Merge surfaces aggressively, merge schemas conservatively.

Follow-up: you're right — as a nav noun it should disappear. It's money-work: a Tasks saved-view ("Collections") and a Money queue. The domain keeps the extra fields and the evidence-gated settle rule; the UI stops asking users to know the word "Follow-up" before finding their work.
Process Run: don't merge into Task — a Run is the occurrence container (its Tasks/Checks/evidence + definition snapshot; OD-11 exists precisely because dated-task-soup loses run-level completion and history). But the word "Process Run" should almost never be an entry point. A barista sees "Today's checklists" on Home/Café; "Runs" as a browsable collection is a manager archive. Rich model, poor surface — like Linear: everything underneath is typed, the user sees "issues."
The rail test: entry points are jobs, ontology appears only inside records.
Signal placement: burying a feed inside Work is a register error — Work is commitments, Signal is news. My recommendation: the feed lives on Home (below the attention brief — open app → what needs me + what's happening, which is how ~30-person ops actually breathes), the composer is everywhere via the launcher, and Work keeps Signals only as archive/search. That needs a one-line amendment to OD-17 (Home gains the feed region), not a new rail destination. If you'd rather have a dedicated feed destination, that's a one-line OD-1 amendment — your call, cheap at mockup phase.

FB-style composer: yes, and it's not even a new decision. OD-42 already says a post requires only content + team + time; category is optional post-capture enrichment. The current long form violates your own locked decision. Text box, photo icon, pills for location/mention, @ fuzzy-match with type badges (Gordi HQ · Site vs Gordi HQ Ops · Team), attention defaulting to FYI as a tap-to-raise pill. Bonus reuse: that same typeahead is the deputy's inline-@ (ADR-0025 D5 gap 1) — one component, two flagship uses.

The plan I propose (one rebuild, not another lap)
This discussion → the ~8 owner calls (below). Not a grill; each question comes with a screenshot or sketch and a recommendation.
I write the Experience Contract (short ADR — it's cross-cutting and binding) + amend the 2–3 OD lines your calls touch.
One shell rebuild against it — salvage what three reviews agree is good (records, fixtures, Money, Inbox, palette, deputy): real routes per collection, collapsible Work group, one page template, job-first entry points, FB-style Signal composer, Home feed.
Validation changes: the static verifier stays as a floor, but acceptance becomes task-based walkthroughs — "as Ayu, report spilled milk; as Rina, find overdue Radiant work" — measured in steps and mis-clicks, plus a convention audit. That's what catches UI mishaps before you do.
Your Phase-0 gate.
On your scope worry (Roastery depth, Standards, an outlet events calendar): that's the strongest argument for the contract. We should not mockup every future surface — we prove the grammar on the six scenarios; then "calendar of events" is just a collection with a calendar view renderer and feed posts, not a new design round. The contract is what makes extensions cheap.

The owner calls I need (each answerable in one line, here in chat): Follow-up demoted to view — yes/no. Run vocabulary at entry points ("Today's checklists" phrasing) — yes/no. Feed on Home vs own destination. FB composer — yes/no. Rail surface budget (~7 top items, Work collapses to one) — yes/no. Verb+object actions ("Start run", "Share update") — yes/no. URL-per-collection — yes/no (this one's really just engineering hygiene; I'd take silence as yes). And one genuinely open one: what should the rail children of Work be, if not eight nouns — my proposal is three: My work · Team work · Library (definitions: Processes/Standards/Objectives), everything else a saved view.

Want to just answer those inline and I'll write the contract + amendments, or push back on any position first?
</AGENT1-A>

and this is for agent 2:
<AGENT2-Q>
i think part of my discomfort is also the amount of different objects / components in the ui. it hsould push for more reusability. what is the difference between task, follow up and process runs? why not all as tasks? then the signal, why not its own rail? or why not at home? why at work? on signal, why the form so lengthy? i'm thinking the signal can take inspiration from a social media (fb) post updates. its simple to post, a text box, an icon to add image, top/bottom of text box there are pills (add location, add mention) and if you type @ in textbox, it pops up a fuzzy match search. the fuzzy match search would have the different category and show the category, so the user is easy to spot eg. Gordi HQ as location / Gordi HQ as team. etc. should  we do another drill-with-docs? but again i dont want another 50+ QnA that ended up not producing what i expected nor prevent the UI mishaps as this has been several iterations to get to this point. I'm also mindful of the fact, this is only mockup phase, we havent actually build this redesign. i havent event touched further aspects of the app, the roastery, the standards, and possible extensions like calendar of events happening around the outlets we managed etc. how to make this merry go round more efficient. lets discuss and plan this first.
</AGENT2-Q>
<AGENT2-A>
You have identified the more fundamental problem: we have been reusing visual styling while exposing too much of the domain model directly in the interface.

“Ruthless typed objects” should make development safer. It should not require every employee to understand every object type.

I would separate three layers:

- Domain contracts: Task, Process Run, Follow-up, Signal, Check, Project, Standard, etc. They may remain distinct where their lifecycle, permissions, audit, or data differs.
- Reusable UI primitives: work item, feed post, definition, record page, list, composer, activity thread.
- User-facing destinations: based on jobs people recognize, not database tables.

For example:

| Domain object | User experience |
|---|---|
| Task | Work item |
| Financial Follow-up | Work item with money-specific fields and settlement controls |
| Task generated by a Process Run | Work item with a “From Café Opening” source |
| Process Run | Execution session containing work items, checks, and evidence |
| Signal | Feed post |
| Process / Standard | Governed definition, mostly hidden from ordinary users |

So I would not literally make Process Runs into Tasks. A Run is closer to an instance of a checklist or workflow: it contains work and maintains a version snapshot. But ordinary users should not need a global “Process Runs” collection. They encounter a Run as “Café opening,” “Monthly close,” or “Stock opname,” and its actionable steps can share the same work-item component as Tasks.

Follow-up is closer to a Task and may eventually become a typed Task extension. It needs special fields and settlement rules, but that does not justify making it a peer navigation concept for everyone.

Your Signal direction is much better than the current prototype:

- A lightweight post composer.
- Text is the primary input.
- Attach image/evidence from an icon.
- Context pills for Team, location, occurrence time, and attention.
- Typing `@` opens grouped fuzzy search results: People, Teams, BUs, and Locations, with clear type labels.
- The current Team/location is prefilled when context makes it safe.
- Category is suggested after posting or available under an optional control.
- Visibility is summarized in one quiet line, not exposed as a lengthy permissions form.
- Task creation happens after posting, from “Create task” on the post.

I also think Signal probably should leave Work. It is communication about what happened, not work itself.

My current recommendation is:

- Home shows the quick composer, relevant recent updates, and attention requiring intervention.
- A top-level **Updates** destination holds the complete Signal feed, search, filters, comments, and history.
- Inbox remains private directed notifications and mentions.
- Work focuses on commitments and execution.
- Modules surface their relevant Runs directly.
- Processes and Standards live behind governance-oriented access rather than appearing beside Tasks for everyone.

That gives users a familiar mental model:

- Home: what matters now?
- Updates: what happened?
- Work: what must be done?
- Inbox: what was directed to me?
- Modules: operate a particular business workflow.
- Money: understand and control financial information.

We should run another documentation drill, but not another exhaustive domain interrogation. I propose a bounded five-decision redesign sprint:

1. User-facing nouns and destinations.
2. Which domain objects collapse into reusable UI families.
3. Updates/Signal capture and consumption.
4. Where governance objects appear and for whom.
5. An extension rule for Calendar, new Modules, and future object types.

After those five decisions, we should create two deliberately different shell prototypes using the same fixtures. We test them against a small set of cold-start tasks before expanding either into the full 23-journey prototype. This prevents us from implementing another complete mockup before discovering that its basic mental model is wrong.

The first decision is foundational:

Should the primary interface be designed for the roughly 90% everyday employee experience—Home, Updates, Work, Inbox, and relevant Modules—while Projects, Processes, Standards, Objectives, and other governance concepts appear progressively only to people who manage them?

My recommendation is yes. This would revise the current assumption that all authorized object collections deserve equal visibility.
</AGENT2-A>

how to proceed and with which agent is better?
```

### assistant

Let me quickly verify Agent-1's OD citations against the decision index before judging — it makes falsifiable claims (OD-42, OD-17, OD-11) that are checkable.

### assistant

Verified Agent-1's citations against your locked decisions — they check out exactly (OD-REDESIGN-42 really does say a Signal post requires only content + team + time + author, so the current long form violates your own locked decision; OD-17, OD-11, OD-1 all cited correctly).

- Financial Follow-up → specialized work item/financial record

Agent 2 also handles progressive disclosure better: ordinary employees should not see every authorized governance collection merely because it exists.

But its recommended top-level `Updates` destination directly conflicts with the locked four-destination rail in [ADR‑0025](/Users/ariefsaid/Coding/gordi-mos/docs/adr/0025-ia-modules-in-rail-redesign-direction.md:693). That could be a valid amendment, but the answer treats it too casually.

Its “two deliberately different shell prototypes” is better than building two complete prototypes, but it still risks beginning another design tournament. You already have enough evidence to narrow the uncertainty more aggressively.

## Positions I recommend locking provisionally

Do not collapse all domain objects into Tasks. Collapse their everyday presentation.

| Concept | Domain position | UI position |
|---|---|---|
| Task | Commitment with PIC, Supervisor, status and due date | Shared work-item presentation |

# SALVAGE-INVENTORY — what each mockup got RIGHT (binding read-first for UI buildout steps)

**Owner rule (2026-07-14, OD-REDESIGN-56):** the mockups are standing reference implementations
with a **presumption of correctness** — anything a mockup answered that is not on the explicit
override list below IS the answer. Builders **port** the reference; re-inventing a surface a mockup
already solved is a review-blocking defect (Experience Contract Rule 11). This file exists because
successive mockup rounds re-did whole surfaces and the right answers got convoluted.

**Precedence when sources disagree:** explicit owner/OD override (list below) → Experience Contract
(`docs/experience-contract.md`) → the mockup that OWNS the surface per this inventory.

Live reference servers (in the `gordi-mos-e7-prototype` working copy,
`docs/design-mockups/redesign-mockups-2026-07/`): e7 shell `python3 serve-e7.py` → :8766/e7-prototype.html ·
convergence flows `python3 convergence-flows/serve-flows.py` → :8134.

## Surface ownership

### e7 shell (`e7-prototype.html` + `e7-views.js` / `e7-records.js` / `e7-data.js` / `e7-prototype.css`) OWNS:

- **Task table / DB-view grammar** — density, columns, grouping, inline grammar. (Owner explicitly
  flagged the convergence table as a wrong re-creation of this.) In the app, the shipped
  `TasksWorkspace`/`TaskSurface` is the code-level canonical; e7 is the visual bar for the redesign skin.
- **⌘K palette as a CENTERED modal popup** — owner explicitly preferred e7's popup over the
  convergence bottom-sheet placement. Port e7's presentation; keep convergence's contents
  (search + Ask Deputy · Share Signal · Create Task, ≤1 contextual).
- **Record pages / renderers** (Task, Signal, Process, Standard, Objective, Follow-up detail
  surfaces), record relations, activity threads.
- **Money surfaces, Inbox (page + quick panel), authorization/persona demonstrations, deputy
  presence, fixtures** (the scenario dataset), and the **visual system**: `--e7-*` tokens, type
  scale, chrome, card/pill/table primitives (all three reviews agreed the visual system is consistent).
  **Token-authority clarifier:** e7's `--e7-*` tokens are the *visual decisions* — app surfaces
  implement those decisions via `DESIGN.md`'s `--ds-*`/`--brand-*`/`--status-*` tokens, whose
  *values* OD-P3-13 already aligned to e7. `--e7-*` names are mockup-internal and must never
  appear in app CSS (there is an active no-leak guard).
- Scenario/journey coverage breadth (the J/Scenario matrix pages).

### convergence flows (`convergence-flows/`) OWNS:

- **The frame** (owner sketch, OD-57): header = logo + breadcrumb · `Search ⌘K` + Inbox + Deputy;
  sidebar = Home / Work ▸ Signals · Tasks · Projects & Processes · Objectives / Events / Money
  [gated, hidden when unauthorized] / Inbox / BU Modules / Admin + profile footer.
- **URL grammar** — canonical route per collection, saved-view + record state in query params,
  Back/refresh/new-tab preservation, redirects, exactly one `aria-current="page"` (parent collapses).
- **FB-style Signal composer** (capture-minimal per OD-42/43; `@` grouped fuzzy with Person/Team/BU
  type badges; Site = location pill; attention FYI tap-to-raise; category post-capture on the card;
  "Create Task" on the POSTED card).
- **Occurrence-as-tasks surfaces** (OD-58): occurrence caption grouping, one-Task-with-checks for
  single-operator checklists, derived roll-up chip, job-function provenance line
  ("PIC: Ayu — via Barista on shift (Café HQ)"), verb+object "Start today's opening".
- **Capture-first phone disclosure** (work before configuration; one "View options" control; bottom
  nav + FAB; ≥44px targets) and the four-region page anatomy with the phone `.ctx-row { top: 0 }` fix.

### `full-redesign-2026-07/` (options a/b/c) — historical IA exploration.

Not wrong, but its open questions were settled by ADR-0025/OD-REDESIGN; consult only for visual
ideas, never for structure.

## The ONLY explicit overrides (owner-said-wrong or audit-confirmed defects — do NOT port these)

From e7:
1. All Work collections sharing one `#/work` URL (Back exited the app) — violates Rule 4.
2. Work parent + child both `aria-current="page"` — violates Rule 5.
3. The 8-collection / 4-heading Work rail — replaced by OD-57's four children.
4. Generic `Create` button fallbacks — Rule 7 verb+object.
5. The long Signal composer form (violated OD-42 capture-minimalism).
6. Mobile Work front-loading three selectors before work — Rule 8.
7. "Process Run" as a user-facing noun / Runs as a browsable entry point — OD-58.
8. Gated "Money•" stub shown to unauthorized viewers on desktop — hide entirely (Rule 9 parity).

From convergence flows:
9. Its re-created task table (use e7's grammar / the app's `TasksWorkspace`).
10. Its bottom-positioned ⌘K palette (use e7's centered modal presentation).
11. `My work · Team work · Library` Work children (superseded by the owner sketch, OD-57; My/Team/
    Overdue live on as saved-view chips inside Tasks).

Anything not on this list that a mockup answers: **the mockup is right — port it.**

export * from './e7-data.js';

   Audit item 4: occurrences surface as TASKS. This is ONE Task carrying a
   single-operator checklist inside it (OD-REDESIGN-12 boundary) — not 12 task
   rows. The roll-up is DERIVED (done/total), never a stored status. The word
   "Process Run" appears nowhere in the UI. The provenance line demonstrates the
   job-function → holder binding (audit item 5 / Q2, OD-REDESIGN-41). */

  type: 'task',
  title: 'Café opening — today',
  teamId: 't_hq_ops',

    { id: 'c8', label: 'Stock cups, lids, napkins', done: false },
    { id: 'c9', label: 'Floor + restroom check', done: false },
  ],
  comments: [],
};

   Owner frame (2026-07-14): Work children are Signals · Tasks · Projects &

};

export const jobSentences = {
  home: 'What needs my attention right now?',
  work: 'Find and do the work I own or my Team owns.',
  tasks: 'Find and do the work I own or my Team owns.',

};

/* Convenience: the live, mutable record index (records + the F2 occurrence). */
export function liveDb() {
  return Object.assign({}, records, { occ_cafe_open_today: cafeOpeningToday });
}

        </AuthProvider>
      </I18nProvider>
    </ThemeProvider>

}

/**
 * job-sentences — Rule 1 registry (one job per rail item).
 *
 * Ported verbatim from the convergence `fixtures.js` `jobSentences` (the
 * Experience Contract Rule-1 table is the authority). `jobSentences` holds the
 * 12 destination/child rows; `jobKeyForPath` resolves a route to its owning
 * job-sentence i18n key (Work child / record → owning type — convergence
 * `contextRow` resolution), so the ContextRow can render the active route's job
 * sentence via `t(jobKeyForPath(pathname))`.
 *
 * No such registry existed in the app before Step 2 (spec §3.1) — genuinely new.
 */
import type { MessageKey } from '@/i18n/messages'

/**
 * The 12 convergence job sentences, keyed by destination/child id. These mirror
 * the i18n `job.*` strings 1:1 (the i18n catalog is the rendered source; this
 * registry is the verbatim port for sanity + Rule-1 traceability).
 */
export const jobSentences = {
  home: 'What needs my attention right now?',
  work: 'Find and do the work I own or my Team owns.',
  tasks: 'Find and do the work I own or my Team owns.',
  signals: 'Search and revisit the Signals your Teams have shared.',
  projects: 'Govern the Processes and Projects that generate the work.',
  objectives: 'Track the Objectives the org committed to.',
  events: "See what's happening around our outlets and when.",
  money: 'Trust the financial figures and act on money exceptions.',
  inbox: 'Triage what asked for me and return to its source.',
  cafe: "Run today's café floor work — openings, checks, stock, shifts.",
  ecommerce: "Fulfil today's online orders against the right stock.",
  roastery: 'Record today’s roasts, yield, and transfers truthfully.',
} as const

/** The union of registry ids. */
export type JobKey = keyof typeof jobSentences

const SEG_TO_JOB: Record<string, MessageKey> = {
  home: 'job.home',
  work: 'job.work',
  tasks: 'job.tasks',
  signals: 'job.signals',
  projects: 'job.projects',
  objectives: 'job.objectives',
  events: 'job.events',
  money: 'job.money',
  inbox: 'job.inbox',
  cafe: 'job.cafe',
  ecommerce: 'job.ecommerce',
  roastery: 'job.roastery',
  profile: 'job.profile',
}

/**
 * Resolve a pathname to its owning job-sentence i18n key (MessageKey).
 *
 * Mirrors the convergence `contextRow` jobKey resolution:
 *  - `/work/:child` → the child's job key (signals/tasks/projects/objectives);
 *    `/work/tasks/:id` (a record) → the owning `tasks` job key.
 *  - `/work` (bare) → `tasks` (Work parent default child).
 *  - top-level destinations + Modules → their own job key.
 *  - `/profile` → `job.profile`.
 *  - unknown (e.g. `/admin/*`, 404) → `job.home` (the always-present fallback).
 */
export function jobKeyForPath(pathname: string): MessageKey {
  const segments = pathname.replace(/^\/+/, '').split('/').filter(Boolean)
  if (segments.length === 0) return 'job.home'

  const root = segments[0]

  // Work → resolve the child (or the record's owning child).
  if (root === 'work') {
    const child = segments[1]
    if (child && SEG_TO_JOB[child]) return SEG_TO_JOB[child]
    // bare /work, or /work/<unknown> → default Work child = tasks
    return 'job.tasks'
  }

  // Module sub-routes resolve to the module job key (e.g. /cafe/log → job.cafe).
  if (SEG_TO_JOB[root]) return SEG_TO_JOB[root]

  // Unknown route → home fallback (context row is minimal on stubs / admin).
  return 'job.home'
}

    46	**Pass if:** every rail entry maps to exactly one row above and the first viewport of its screen answers
    47	that job before any configuration. **Fail if:** any rail entry has no single job sentence, or two entries
    48	share a job (duplicate Home/Dashboard/Operate/Plan), or a screen buries its job behind selectors/empty
    49	state.
    50	
    51	## Rule 2 — Three-layer boundary: domain contract → UI family → destination (surfaces merge, schemas don't)
    52	
    53	Every rendered surface is composed from **reusable UI families** over **typed, distinct domain contracts**,
    54	assembled into **job-first destinations**. Merging of *surfaces* is aggressive; merging of *schemas* is
    55	conservative (no Blueprint, no freeform data — OD-REDESIGN-29 / D16).
    56	
    57	| Domain contract (typed, distinct) | Reusable UI family | Job-first destination |
    58	|---|---|---|
    59	| **Task** | work item (row/card) + record page + activity thread | Work → My work / Team work; Module queues |
    60	| **Signal** | feed post + composer + mention pill | Home feed (ambient) / Work archive-search / Signal record page |
    61	| **Process / Standard / Objective / Project** *(governed definitions)* | governed-definition page + guided designer | Work → Library |
    62	| **Process occurrence** *(thin Run record)* | grouped task list under an occurrence caption + roll-up | Work occurrence grouping; Home attention |
    63	| **Follow-up** | work item (money-shaped) + record page | Money queue entry; Work Tasks saved-view |
    64	| **Check / Exception** | activity-thread entry / exception card | Process occurrence view; Home attention |
    65	| **Inbox item** | triage row | Inbox (page + quick panel) |
    66	| **Person / Team / BU** | mention pill / scope chip | composer; record context row |
    67	
    68	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-16/29 / D2/D3a/D3d/D7/D16. Q2 (function→holder) adds "job function" as a
    69	template binding that resolves to a Person UI family at spawn — the schema stays Task-shaped.*
    70	
    71	**Pass if:** each destination row is built only from families in column 2 over contracts in column 1, and
    72	no two contracts share a renderer that erases their type boundary (a Signal is never rendered as a Task, a
    73	Follow-up never as a generic Task without its money fields). **Fail if:** a new screen introduces a
    74	one-off record editor, embeds a duplicate record (D3a violation), or copies a value that should be linked
    75	(anchor A8).
    76	
    77	## Rule 3 — Rail / surface budget (numeric caps)
    78	
    79	The rail and each surface obey fixed numeric budgets; growth is by **collection + view renderer + feed
    80	posts**, never by new rail roots or new anatomies (see Rule 10).
    81	
    82	| Budget | Cap |
    83	|---|---|
    84	| Destination roots in the rail | **5** (Home · Work · Events · Money *[gated]* · Inbox) — Events added by owner frame directive 2026-07-14 (amends OD-REDESIGN-1 / D1). **RATIFIED** by the owner's frame sketch (OD-REDESIGN-57) and shipped in the rail — not a pending slot |
    85	| Module roots | **3** initially (Café · Ecommerce · Roastery) |
    86	| BU group headings above Modules | **2** (Retail Ops · B2B Ops) |
    87	| Utility entries in the rail | **2** (Admin Settings · Personal Profile), gated, in their own group — never a destination zone |
    88	| Work collection-switcher children | **4** (Signals · Tasks · Projects & Processes · Objectives) — owner frame directive 2026-07-14 after seeing the My work · Team work · Library variant rendered; My/Team/Overdue become saved-view chips inside Tasks |
    89	| Family headings inside any collection switcher | **0** (flat; groups collapsed) |
    90	| Contextual actions on any one screen (besides the Action Launcher) | **1** (OD-REDESIGN-46 / D32) |
    91	| `aria-current="page"` on the whole document | **1** (see Rule 5) |
    92	
    93	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-1/23 / D1/D3f, OD-REDESIGN-46 / D32, OD-REDESIGN-20 / D1.*
    94	
    95	**Pass if:** every numeric cap holds at desktop and on phone. **Fail if:** any cap is exceeded, or a
    96	destination/Module is duplicated, or the Work switcher re-sprouts family headings / >3 children.
    97	
    98	## Rule 4 — Canonical routes + URL state semantics
    99	
   100	*Clarified by OD-REDESIGN-63 (2026-07-15): in-list click opens the split drawer (fast triage); direct/new-tab/refresh opens the same content as a standalone full canonical page. Both — the drawer is retained.*
   101	
   102	Every collection and saved view has a **canonical route**; view/presentation state lives in **URL query
   103	params**; Back / refresh / bookmark / new-tab all preserve location.
   104	
   105	- Collection route shape: `#/work/tasks`, `#/work/team`, `#/work/library`, `#/money`, `#/inbox`, …
   106	- Saved-view + presentation state as query params: `?view=mine&status=open&layout=board&group=team`.
   107	- A first-class record has one canonical URL (OD-REDESIGN-7 / D3a): normal click → shared Record Panel;
   108	  new-tab / direct URL / refresh → full canonical page; same renderer, `mode="panel" | "page"`.
   109	- Phone panel-stack semantics become page-stack semantics **without changing URLs or Back behavior**
   110	  (`PROTOTYPE-BRIEF.md` §8).
   111	
   112	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-7/19 / D3a/D3d. Fixes the confirmed defect where every Work collection shares
   113	`#/work` and refresh loses the collection.*
   114	
   115	**Pass if:** on any collection/view, copying the URL into a new tab renders the same collection, saved
   116	view, filters, and layout; browser Back and panel Back each pop exactly one level; deep-linking a record
   117	opens its canonical page. **Fail if:** two collections share one URL, or any navigation mutates state
   118	without updating the URL, or Back exits the app.
   119	
   120	## Rule 5 — One current location (exactly one `aria-current="page"`)
   121	
   122	At any moment, **exactly one** element in the document carries `aria-current="page"`. When a child
   123	location is active (e.g. Work → My work), the child carries `page` and the parent collapses to
   124	`aria-current="location"` (or none). Parent and child are **never** simultaneously `page`; sibling groups
   125	never co-activate.
   126	
   127	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-7/19 / D3a (one canonical location). Fixes the confirmed defect where the
   128	Work parent and active Work child both announce `page`.*
   129	
   130	**Pass if:** a DOM query for `[aria-current="page"]` returns exactly one element on every route, desktop
   131	and phone. **Fail if:** it returns zero or more than one.
   132	
   133	## Rule 6 — One page anatomy per route
   134	
   135	Every route renders the same four-region anatomy: **(1) header → (2) context row → (3) content region →
   136	(4) record drawer** (the shared right-panel host, D3b). The header carries brand + current-location
   137	breadcrumb (left) and the ⌘K search field + Inbox + Deputy (right) — universal actions (Ask Deputy ·
   138	Share Signal · Create Task) live in the ⌘K palette, not as header buttons (owner frame directive
   139	2026-07-14); the context row carries scope (Person/Team/BU) + the route's job sentence;
   140	the content region holds the collection/list/feed; the drawer holds the stack-navigated record, Inbox
   141	quick triage, or deputy — never competing drawers.
   142	
   143	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-2/16 / D2/D3a/D3b/D7. Phone collapses header + context row into a compact
   144	sticky bar and the drawer becomes a page stack, but the four roles persist.*
   145	
   146	**Pass if:** each of the 4 regions is identifiable on every route, and no route invents a fifth region or
   147	a second drawer host. **Fail if:** a route re-invents its own chrome, nests a physical drawer inside the
   148	record drawer, or omits the context row's job/scope.
   149	
   150	## Rule 7 — Verb+object action grammar (no bare `Create`)
   151	
   152	Every visible primary action is **verb+object** and names the current job: *"Start today's opening"*,
   153	*"Share Signal"*, *"Add follow-up"*, *"Run check"*, *"Log roast"*, *"Create Task"*, *"Draft Process"*.
   154	A bare **`Create`** is forbidden. The Action Launcher keeps its universal actions stable (Share Signal ·
   155	Ask Deputy/dictate · Create Task · More) plus **at most one** contextual action (OD-REDESIGN-46 / D32);
   156	⌘K, the desktop `+ Create`, the phone `+` FAB, and the deputy all dispatch the same commands.
   157	
   158	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-21/46 / D10/D32. Fixes the confirmed defect where several Work collections
   159	fall back to a generic `Create`.*
   160	
   161	**Pass if:** every primary button, FAB contextual action, and Launcher entry is verb+object and names the
   162	job; the Launcher shows ≤1 contextual action alongside the stable universal set. **Fail if:** any visible
   163	action is a bare `Create`/`Add`/`New`, or the Launcher algorithmically reorders its universal actions.
   164	
   165	## Rule 8 — Capture-first disclosure (mobile first)
   166	
   167	*Refined by OD-REDESIGN-61 (2026-07-15): capture-first binds the primary/least-technical persona surface; a MANAGER persona may default to a denser filter view. Role-scoped, not weakened.*
   168	
   169	On phone, **work appears before configuration.** A user opening any collection sees their work items in
   170	the first viewport; the collection picker, saved-view selector, and view-as/presentation controls collapse
   171	behind a **single** control. The composer (Rule: OD-REDESIGN-42 / D28) opens with only *content + owning
   172	Team + occurrence time + author*; category, attention, and mentions are post-capture enrichments on
   173	compact pills. Tap targets ≥44px; dense tables collapse to mobile record lists, never clipped grids.
   174	
   175	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-42/43/46 / D28/D29/D32 and `PROTOTYPE-BRIEF.md` §8. Fixes the confirmed
   176	defect where mobile Work front-loads three selectors before showing work, and the Signal composer is a
   177	long form.*
   178	
   179	**Pass if:** on a ≤390px viewport, the first viewport of every collection shows at least one work item
   180	(not only selectors), all view-configuration controls are behind one affordance, and the Signal composer's
   181	initial fields are exactly the four capture-minimal fields. **Fail if:** any phone screen leads with
   182	configuration, or the composer demands category/attention before it will accept a post.
   183	
   184	## Rule 9 — Responsive disclosure order (desktop mirrors mobile in meaning, not in density)
   185	
   186	Desktop supports dense review (multi-column tables, board/timeline, inline cell editing, persistent
   187	rail + panel); phone supports fast execution/capture. The **information hierarchy and command meanings stay
   188	identical** across form factors — only density and the disclosure mechanism change. Phone uses bottom
   189	navigation for the most relevant destinations, with remaining destinations and Modules behind a
   190	conventional menu; no desktop rail squeezed into mobile.
   191	
   192	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-46 / D32, `PROTOTYPE-BRIEF.md` §8, and `docs/jtbd.md` §6 "Responsive access."*
   193	
   194	**Pass if:** the same job is completable on phone and desktop with the same action names and the same
   195	reachable records; phone bottom-nav + menu cover every rail entry the viewer is authorised for; inline-edit
   196	commit contract (Enter/Tab/click-outside saves, Escape discards — OD-REDESIGN-22 / D3c) is identical on
   197	both. **Fail if:** a phone user cannot reach an authorised record/action, or copy/action meaning drifts
   198	between form factors, or a desktop rail is horizontally squeezed onto phone.
   199	
   200	## Rule 10 — The extension test (a new Module / calendar / record type ships without a new rail root or new anatomy)
   201	
   202	A new Module (e.g. a future HR/Procurement Module), a calendar surface, or a new record type ships by
   203	adding **(i) a collection + (ii) a view renderer + (iii) feed posts / activity-thread entries** — reusing
   204	the existing UI families (Rule 2) and the existing page anatomy (Rule 6). It must **not** require a new
   205	rail *root*, a new *destination* job that duplicates an existing one, a new *page anatomy*, or a new
   206	*drawer host*.
   207	
   208	*Operationalises OD-REDESIGN-1/15/29 / D1/D9/D16. Modules earn a rail root only via the BU-grouped
   209	workflow-coherence test (D1); until then they live as collections/views inside Work. (Events was
   210	promoted to a rail root by explicit owner directive 2026-07-14 — that is the owner exercising the
   211	amendment path, not a Rule-10 violation; the rule still binds every future addition.)*
   212	
   213	**Pass if:** a reviewer can describe how to add "a Standards compliance calendar" or "a future Procurement
   214	Module" using only the three additions above, with no contract change. **Fail if:** adding the surface
   215	forces a new rail root outside the BU-grouped Module rule, a new page anatomy, a second drawer, or a
   216	duplicate destination job — that means **the contract is being violated**, not extended.
   217	
   218	---
   219	
   220	## How this contract is scored
   221	
   222	- Every flow review (S1–S6 in `PROTOTYPE-BRIEF.md`) and every four-lens design review records **pass/fail
   223	  per rule**, citing the screen + viewport. A single **fail** is a blocking defect on par with a
   224	  `docs/jtbd.md` calibration anchor (A1–A14).
   225	- Rules 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 also fix **confirmed defects in the current shell** (single-`#/work` URL;
   226	  co-active `aria-current`; generic `Create`; mobile selector-stacking; long-form composer; 8-collection
   227	  Work rail). Those must visibly pass before owner approval.
   228	- Rules 2, 6, 9, 10 are the **anti-re-invention** guardrails: they exist so the next build round does not
   229	  re-invent the UI grammar — which is the root cause this sprint was opened to fix.
   230	- Pending ratification: Rule 1's Signal-home row and Rule 2's Signal UI-family placement assume **Q1 =
   230	- Pending ratification: Rule 1's Signal-home row and Rule 2's Signal UI-family placement assume **Q1 =
   231	  APPROVE**; Rule 2's "job function" note assumes **Q2 = APPROVE** (see `CONVERGENCE-AUDIT.md`). A "no" on
   232	  either removes only the affected clause; the rest of the contract stands.
   233	
   234	## Rule 11 — Component reuse (added 2026-07-14, owner-directed after the mockup lesson)
   235	
   236	A builder may **never re-implement a surface or component that already exists** in `mos-app`
   237	**or in a mockup reference**. Extend, re-home, or PORT the existing one. The mockups carry a
   238	**presumption of correctness** (OD-REDESIGN-56): which mockup owns which surface, and the only
   239	explicit overrides, is `docs/design-mockups/redesign-mockups-2026-07/SALVAGE-INVENTORY.md` —
   240	binding read-first for every UI step. The shipped
   241	Tasks DB-view (`TasksWorkspace` / `TaskSurface` / drawer — ADR-0007/0008), the record-panel host,
   242	pickers, and any component under `mos-app/src/components/` are the canonical implementations.
   243	
   244	*Why this rule exists: during the mockup phase each iteration re-created components (task table,
   245	⌘K palette) and quality drifted randomly — the owner caught it. In the app, re-implementation is a
   246	review-blocking defect.*
   247	
   248	**Pass if:** the diff extends/moves existing components; any new component demonstrably has no
   249	existing counterpart. **Fail if:** a new implementation duplicates an existing surface's job, even
   250	"temporarily".
   251	
   252	## Rule 12 — Usable by a high-school graduate with no training (added 2026-07-15, owner-directed)
   253	
   254	*TWO FRONTS (OD-REDESIGN-66): Rule 12 is scored as the **member/least-technical persona**. It does NOT
   255	license dumbing down the **manager** front, which needs efficiency + density (filters, dense review
   256	tables). Role-adaptive disclosure (OD-REDESIGN-61) serves both. A review must judge BOTH fronts.*
   257	
   258	The bar is **not** "a power user can figure it out" — it is **"a Gordi staff member with a
   259	high-school education and zero training completes the job on the first try, unaided."** Usability and
   260	speed beat model completeness and feature richness (CLAUDE.md charter). This rule is scored by a
   261	**task-based cold-start walkthrough**, not by taste alone.
   262	
   263	**Concretely, on every screen:**
   264	- **Plain language, no system vocabulary.** UI never exposes internal object names or jargon a
   265	  barista wouldn't say. "Today's opening checklist," not "Process Run"; "Share an update," not "emit
   266	  a Signal." (Reinforces OD-58, Rule 7.)
   267	- **The primary action is obvious without instruction** — one clear next step per screen, not a wall
   268	  of equal-weight options.
   269	- **Recognition over recall** — labels + icons the user recognizes; never require memorizing codes,
   270	  paths, or which internal collection holds their work.
   271	- **No configuration before the goal** — the user sees their work/does the job first; setup and
   272	  options are optional and secondary (Rule 8 capture-first).
   273	- **Helper text compensates for nothing** — if a screen needs a paragraph explaining what an object
   274	  is, the entry point is wrong. Fix the entry point, don't add prose.
   275	
   276	**Pass if:** in a cold-start walkthrough of the step's job (as the least technical persona — a Café
   277	barista/member, not an admin), the user (a) identifies the starting point unaided, (b) completes the
   278	job, (c) hits no unexplained noun, (d) always sees an obvious next action, in a reasonable step count
   279	with no backtracking. **Fail if:** any of those breaks — measured, recorded in the ledger, not vibed.
   280	
   281	*Oracle: `docs/jtbd.md` (the job each screen must serve) + `docs/reference/twenty-ixd-patterns.md`
   282	(the "ruthless reuse → familiar grammar" target). Reusable grammar IS an ease-of-use lever: a user
   283	who learns one screen already knows the next.*

   252	## Rule 12 — Usable by a high-school graduate with no training (added 2026-07-15, owner-directed)
   253	
   254	*TWO FRONTS (OD-REDESIGN-66): Rule 12 is scored as the **member/least-technical persona**. It does NOT
   255	license dumbing down the **manager** front, which needs efficiency + density (filters, dense review
   256	tables). Role-adaptive disclosure (OD-REDESIGN-61) serves both. A review must judge BOTH fronts.*
   257	
   258	The bar is **not** "a power user can figure it out" — it is **"a Gordi staff member with a
   259	high-school education and zero training completes the job on the first try, unaided."** Usability and
   260	speed beat model completeness and feature richness (CLAUDE.md charter). This rule is scored by a
   261	**task-based cold-start walkthrough**, not by taste alone.
   262	
   263	**Concretely, on every screen:**
   264	- **Plain language, no system vocabulary.** UI never exposes internal object names or jargon a
   265	  barista wouldn't say. "Today's opening checklist," not "Process Run"; "Share an update," not "emit
   266	  a Signal." (Reinforces OD-58, Rule 7.)
   267	- **The primary action is obvious without instruction** — one clear next step per screen, not a wall
   268	  of equal-weight options.
   269	- **Recognition over recall** — labels + icons the user recognizes; never require memorizing codes,
   270	  paths, or which internal collection holds their work.
   271	- **No configuration before the goal** — the user sees their work/does the job first; setup and
   272	  options are optional and secondary (Rule 8 capture-first).
   273	- **Helper text compensates for nothing** — if a screen needs a paragraph explaining what an object
   274	  is, the entry point is wrong. Fix the entry point, don't add prose.
   275	
   276	**Pass if:** in a cold-start walkthrough of the step's job (as the least technical persona — a Café
   277	barista/member, not an admin), the user (a) identifies the starting point unaided, (b) completes the
   278	job, (c) hits no unexplained noun, (d) always sees an obvious next action, in a reasonable step count
   279	with no backtracking. **Fail if:** any of those breaks — measured, recorded in the ledger, not vibed.
   280	
   281	*Oracle: `docs/jtbd.md` (the job each screen must serve) + `docs/reference/twenty-ixd-patterns.md`
   282	(the "ruthless reuse → familiar grammar" target). Reusable grammar IS an ease-of-use lever: a user
   283	who learns one screen already knows the next.*

(`docs/reviews/feat-redesign-buildout.md`) is the evidence of record; this file is the index over it.
If the two disagree, **the ledger is ground truth** — and this file is stale: fix it.

## Mode (READ THIS FIRST — it changes what you're allowed to do)

- `mos-app/src/components/tasks/tasks-workspace.tsx:531-537`, `mos-app/src/components/tasks/task-surface.tsx:627-630` — saved-view parsing is centralized, but search-param composition is still somewhat spread. Not a functional defect on its own, but it falls a bit short of the stated “centralize URLSearchParams logic” goal. A tiny shared helper for collection/search-param merging would keep this seam tighter.

### Overall assessment
**BLOCK** — the spec mapping and rewire-first implementation are largely right, but Rule 4 is not fully met because several real record-open paths still drop `?view=`. Fix those search-blind links and align the tests, then this should be ready to approve.

REVIEW-DONE

## Step 3 — Tasks re-home (spec + code-quality, gpt-5.4 cross-family)

**Verdict: BLOCK** (1 finding). Saved-view URL grammar + Rule-11 reuse are sound (only use-tasks-saved-view.ts new; DAL/workspace/drawer rewired), but Rule-4 `?view=` preservation is INCOMPLETE — fixed on row-click, dropped on 3 other open paths:
- task-row.tsx:81 (task-name Link)
- row-menu.tsx:36 (row-menu Open)
- mobile-grouped-cards.tsx:84 (mobile card open)
So new-tab/name-link/row-menu/mobile open lose the saved view. Fix + per-path test required.

### Step 3 — BLOCK resolution (fix round gpt-5.4 + Director verify, 2026-07-15)

The 3 record-open paths now thread `search: recordSearch` (commit fdee22e):
- task-row.tsx (name Link, via `recordTo`) + passes recordSearch to RowMenu
- row-menu.tsx (Open) — `to={{pathname, search: recordSearch}}`
- mobile-grouped-cards.tsx — same
Re-verify: typecheck clean · 2592 unit green · saved-view + split-view e2e 7/7. Director live-confirmed
the name-link preserves `?view=overdue` on open. **Step-3 verdict now: APPROVE.** Owner visual sign-off
+ walkthrough pending (AFK).

## Design/UX review — steps 1–3 (Luna, autonomous)

**Overall: BLOCK.** The warm palette, shell header, saved-view URL wiring, centered command palette, and
role-gated rail are solid. The rendered product is not yet the owner-approved redesign experience: Home
still exposes the retired cadence model, mobile Tasks violates capture-first disclosure, the Task record
leaks RACI onto a Task and has no obvious completion action, and one phone route has zero current-location
markers. These are contract failures, not polish nits.

### Review method and evidence

I started with `docs/experience-contract.md` Rules 1–12, `docs/jtbd.md`, and
`docs/reference/twenty-ixd-patterns.md`, then read `SALVAGE-INVENTORY.md` before opening mockups. I used
fresh named browser sessions, verified **Gordi MOS** branding (not PMO Portal), and inspected:

- Built app: `http://localhost:5173/mos/`, Cafe Ops at 1280×900 and 390×844; Director at 1280×900.
- Mockups: `http://localhost:8766/e7-prototype.html` and `http://localhost:8134/` at both widths.
- Built surfaces: Home, `/work/tasks?view=mine|team|overdue|followups`, the centered ⌘K palette,
  `/work/tasks/:id?view=...`, phone More, `/work/signals`, and `/cafe`.
- Mechanical checks: URL/query preservation, `aria-current`, responsive widths, palette focus/dialog
  semantics, rail gating, and direct record navigation. Captures are in the temporary
  `/tmp/gordi-review/` directory.

### Lens (a) — Visual / correctness: **FAIL**

**What passes**

- Step 1's warm cream surfaces, navy/blue action color, restrained borders, type scale, and low-depth
  shadows read as the same Quiet Control Surface identity. I saw no purple wash, generic gradient, or
  token-slop tell.
- The desktop and phone shell are coherent: brand, breadcrumb, Search, Inbox, Deputy, context row,
  bottom nav, and More are visually consistent.
- The built ⌘K palette is correctly centered (`role=dialog`, `aria-modal=true`, focused combobox):
  560px wide at desktop and inset at phone. Its actions are visibly ordered **Ask Deputy · Share Signal
  · Create Task**.
- Cafe Ops correctly does not see Money or Admin; Director sees the full authorized rail.

**Findings**

- **Home is visually the old app, not the reference Home.** Cafe Ops sees “Your week at a glance”,
  KPI cards, a large legacy task table, “My weekly update”, and “Today on the Daily Log”. Director sees
  `—` revenue/margin cards and “No snapshot yet · next sync 03:30 WIB”, which is a dead cockpit state,
  not an attention brief. The e7/convergence reference puts consequence-ordered attention first.
- **Tasks is horizontally over-dense at desktop.** At 1280px the old table has an internal 1,284px
  scroll surface inside a 994px content area; the right-side Due/Activity columns are cut from the first
  view. The e7 task table fits the decision columns (Title, Ownership, Supervisor, Status, Due) in one
  calm review surface.
- **Rendered fixtures are not production-like Gordi records.** The first rows are named
  `URL row-menu 1784062219837`, `URL overdue 1784062211102`, `E2E Archiveable Task`, and `AC-305…`.

after step 11).

## Verdicts

<!-- Machine-read by scripts/pre-merge-check.sh. Last line per review wins. -->
<!-- Consolidated: every step's battery is APPROVE in its own ledger; the lines below summarize the
     branch-wide outcome. Steps with BLOCK→fix→APPROVE cycles: 4 (design: unstyled surfaces;
     security: HIGH-1), 5 (design: Rule-8 phone), 6 (design: due-list flood; pending re-review below). -->

- spec: APPROVE — per-step spec reviews (opus), 2026-07-16/17: steps 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 all
  APPROVE with AC-by-AC coverage tables in the step ledgers; every AC owned by one test at its layer.
- code-quality: APPROVE — per-step code-quality reviews (opus): steps 4–11 all APPROVE; step-6
  fix-then-ship items (silent write failures, useOccurrenceGroups extraction) FIXED and verified.
- design: APPROVE — all eight steps. Steps 4, 5, 6 each BLOCK→fix→re-review APPROVE with rendered
  evidence (step 6's manager front re-scored 4/10→8.5/10); steps 7, 8, 9, 10 first-pass APPROVE.
  HOLISTIC cross-module pass (final visual/regression, 3 personas × 2 breakpoints): SHIP — one
  grammar confirmed, retired surfaces absent everywhere (rail/⌘K/routes), F1/F2/F3 frictionless at
  390px, table-density convention holds. Its 2 Important + 2 copy minors fixed in 785cdf3 (Deputy
  retired-noun chip, catalog Add composes its noun, Money H1, NotFound link).
- security: APPROVE — security-auditor (opus): step 4 BLOCK (HIGH-1 + 3 Low) → all empirically
  CLEARED; step 6 APPROVE (0 Critical/High; Low-1/2/3 hardened in the fix wave, re-verified by
  pgTAP). Steps 5/7/8/9/10/11 carry no new auth/RLS/schema surface beyond those audits' scope.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | PASS — 0 errors |
| `npm run lint -- --max-warnings=0` (eslint + stylelint) | PASS — 0 |

| `supabase test db` (pgTAP) | PASS — 100 files / 727 tests |

| `bash scripts/pre-merge-check.sh` | **PASS — exit 0** (all required reviews cleared; run 2026-07-17 at branch close) |

## Ratify before merge (consolidated — the owner's one post-step-11 list)

Every conservative default taken while the owner was absent, with its home ledger:
1. **Q1 Signal-on-Home** — provisionally approved (OD-REDESIGN-59); built as specified. (step 4)
2. **`can_read_signal` SECURITY DEFINER** — deviation from ADR-0050 D4 (INVOKER recurses); ratify into the ADR. (step 4)
3. **`comments_select` signal tightening** — reader-of-parent SELECT gate. (step 4)
4. **A7 fixture role-strip reading** of AC-403/406 (Team membership alone ≠ read under BU-scoped R2). (step 4)
5. **Attention pill not built** (spec §4 had no owning AC) — defer vs follow-up. (step 4)
6. **Record surface panel-only** (page-mode branch unbuilt). (step 4)
7. **"Owning Team" / "Occurred at" composer labels** — spec-literal wording kept; plain-language rename optional. (step 4)
8. **Region-order store = localStorage** (profile column later) + inline Home toggle + "My items first" wording. (step 5)
9. **Step-6 RATIFY-1..10** — extend work_lines; WIB period keys; explicit-Start no-scheduler; shallow supervisor resolution; ops_lead+admin `process.start`; org-readable runs; pending-never-guess; idempotency grain; human completion; OD-12 checklist boundary. (step 6)
10. **Step-7 RATIFY-7A..7F** — members cannot start the opening (7A, the load-bearing café call); no kitchen-schema bridge (7B); dev-seed-only binding (7C); /cafe as Café home (7D — shipped); capability mirror (7E); name-based process resolution (7F). (step 7)
11. **RATIFY-8A ⌘K-only catalog access on phone** — Option A implemented and design-endorsed. (step 8)
12. **SHOW_FOLLOWUPS stays false** (backup/restore go-live gate); Door-2 minimal link pending its flag-on design review. (step 9)
13. **Events placeholder copy** (rewritten post-review — final wording yours) + quiet archetype. (step 10)
14. **Modules stay in the rail** — Director default; override window open until merge. (inherited)
15. **AC-013 footer wording** amendment (security HIGH-1 era). (inherited from base)

## Deferred debt (tracked, non-blocking)

- Signals feed/archive pagination before volume grows (step 4 CQ). Fan-out concurrent-uncommitted
  race (B2B-era). `due_process_runs` weekly/monthly surfacing + scale. Assign-dialog focus-trap
  (house overlay debt). Dedicated café-lead e2e persona (replaces the shared-persona grant).
  FR-708 deep-link as rendered link (currently description text). Step-10 phone ⌘K launcher
  affordance polish.

## Review

- **Correct:** Rail structure, gated destinations, Home attention-first ordering, Tasks reuse, occurrence grouping, and mobile Tasks disclosure align with E7 ownership and Rules 3/8/11. `mos-app/src/shell/rail-nav.tsx:103-129`, `mos-app/src/components/tasks/tasks-workspace.tsx:120-121,731-755`.
- **Correct:** Signal composer supports capture-minimal fields and grouped Person/Team/BU mentions. `mos-app/src/components/signals/signal-composer.tsx:132-196`.
- **Blocker — confirmed, high confidence:** Signal direct URLs always open a drawer, violating OD-63/Rule 4’s direct/new-tab/refresh full-page semantics. `mos-app/src/pages/signals-archive-page.tsx:163-172`; contrasting Task implementation: `mos-app/src/pages/tasks-layout.tsx:56-85`. This is explicitly listed as deferred/ratify item 6 in `docs/reviews/claude-redesign-buildout-completion-vdrd17.md:62-64`.
- **Blocker — confirmed, high confidence:** Signal archive mobile places search and retracted controls before the Signal list, with no single “View options” disclosure. `mos-app/src/pages/signals-archive-page.tsx:105-125`; Rule 8 requires work before configuration and one collapsed control (`docs/experience-contract.md:169-182`).
- **Important — confirmed, high confidence:** Context row renders a generic role-area (“Café”, “Finance”, etc.), not Person/Team/BU scope. `mos-app/src/shell/context-row.tsx:6-14,29-46`. The standing reference renders avatar/person plus location scope (`convergence-flows/flows.js:363-379`), required by Rule 6 (`docs/experience-contract.md:135-148`).
- **Important — confirmed, high confidence:** Tasks’ primary action is `+ New task`, not verb+object `Create Task`. `mos-app/src/components/tasks/tasks-workspace.tsx:714-721`; copy source `mos-app/src/i18n/messages.ts:125-139`. This violates Rule 7 (`docs/experience-contract.md:150-163`).
- **Important — confirmed, high confidence:** Approved Signal composer controls were dropped: convergence owns location/time/attention pills and an attach-evidence action (`convergence-flows/flows.js:450-461`), while app composer only renders a derived site text pill and no attention or attachment control (`mos-app/src/components/signals/signal-composer.tsx:155-198`). The missing attention pill is explicitly recorded as deferred in the completion ledger (`...completion-vdrd17.md:62`).
- **Note — confirmed scope:** Ecommerce/Roastery remain stubs and Events is intentionally an empty extension surface; these are deferred/explicit Step 10–11 scope, not regressions (`mos-app/src/router.tsx:159-161`, `mos-app/src/pages/events-page.tsx:22-29`, `docs/plans/2026-07-14-redesign-buildout.md:51-55`).
- **Note — two fronts:** Tasks correctly distinguishes member capture-first from manager density (`mos-app/src/components/tasks/tasks-workspace.tsx:120-121`). Signals archive does not role-adapt its mobile controls, so the member front fails Rule 8 while manager efficiency is preserved.
- **Residual architecture risk:** Shell, Task route, Signal archive, Signal composer, and Deputy each mount separate drawer surfaces (`mos-app/src/shell/app-shell.tsx:81-98`, `mos-app/src/pages/signals-archive-page.tsx:166-170`, `mos-app/src/shell/signal-composer-host.tsx:76-100`). This conflicts with the single shared drawer-host contract (`docs/experience-contract.md:135-148`), though the completion ledger treats this area as deferred rather than newly introduced scope.

## Review

- **Correct:** Rail structure, gated destinations, Home attention-first ordering, Tasks reuse, occurrence grouping, and mobile Tasks disclosure align with E7 ownership and Rules 3/8/11. `mos-app/src/shell/rail-nav.tsx:103-129`, `mos-app/src/components/tasks/tasks-workspace.tsx:120-121,731-755`.
- **Correct:** Signal composer supports capture-minimal fields and grouped Person/Team/BU mentions. `mos-app/src/components/signals/signal-composer.tsx:132-196`.
- **Blocker — confirmed, high confidence:** Signal direct URLs always open a drawer, violating OD-63/Rule 4’s direct/new-tab/refresh full-page semantics. `mos-app/src/pages/signals-archive-page.tsx:163-172`; contrasting Task implementation: `mos-app/src/pages/tasks-layout.tsx:56-85`. This is explicitly listed as deferred/ratify item 6 in `docs/reviews/claude-redesign-buildout-completion-vdrd17.md:62-64`.
- **Blocker — confirmed, high confidence:** Signal archive mobile places search and retracted controls before the Signal list, with no single “View options” disclosure. `mos-app/src/pages/signals-archive-page.tsx:105-125`; Rule 8 requires work before configuration and one collapsed control (`docs/experience-contract.md:169-182`).
- **Important — confirmed, high confidence:** Context row renders a generic role-area (“Café”, “Finance”, etc.), not Person/Team/BU scope. `mos-app/src/shell/context-row.tsx:6-14,29-46`. The standing reference renders avatar/person plus location scope (`convergence-flows/flows.js:363-379`), required by Rule 6 (`docs/experience-contract.md:135-148`).
- **Important — confirmed, high confidence:** Tasks’ primary action is `+ New task`, not verb+object `Create Task`. `mos-app/src/components/tasks/tasks-workspace.tsx:714-721`; copy source `mos-app/src/i18n/messages.ts:125-139`. This violates Rule 7 (`docs/experience-contract.md:150-163`).
- **Important — confirmed, high confidence:** Approved Signal composer controls were dropped: convergence owns location/time/attention pills and an attach-evidence action (`convergence-flows/flows.js:450-461`), while app composer only renders a derived site text pill and no attention or attachment control (`mos-app/src/components/signals/signal-composer.tsx:155-198`). The missing attention pill is explicitly recorded as deferred in the completion ledger (`...completion-vdrd17.md:62`).
- **Note — confirmed scope:** Ecommerce/Roastery remain stubs and Events is intentionally an empty extension surface; these are deferred/explicit Step 10–11 scope, not regressions (`mos-app/src/router.tsx:159-161`, `mos-app/src/pages/events-page.tsx:22-29`, `docs/plans/2026-07-14-redesign-buildout.md:51-55`).
- **Note — two fronts:** Tasks correctly distinguishes member capture-first from manager density (`mos-app/src/components/tasks/tasks-workspace.tsx:120-121`). Signals archive does not role-adapt its mobile controls, so the member front fails Rule 8 while manager efficiency is preserved.
- **Residual architecture risk:** Shell, Task route, Signal archive, Signal composer, and Deputy each mount separate drawer surfaces (`mos-app/src/shell/app-shell.tsx:81-98`, `mos-app/src/pages/signals-archive-page.tsx:166-170`, `mos-app/src/shell/signal-composer-host.tsx:76-100`). This conflicts with the single shared drawer-host contract (`docs/experience-contract.md:135-148`), though the completion ledger treats this area as deferred rather than newly introduced scope.
